newsitem.title: LATVIA: Latvian stocks lose ground amid higher activity.
newsitem.headline: Latvian stocks lose ground amid higher activity.

text.p: Latvian blue chips mostly lost ground amid slightly higher activity, among them leading stock Unibanka, which was the most traded on Friday, dealers said.
Total turnover came to 219,000 lats versus 173,000 and the Rietumu Bank index closed 0.88 percent off at 226.17.
Unibanka slipped back to 4.75 lats from 4.80 on large volume of 112,000 lats before the deadline of April 7 for registering 1996 dividends and bonus shares.
"Activity was slightly higher today compared to yesterday, but not much is happening," said one dealer.
"The market was calm today and rather boring," Uldis Bulavs, a dealer of Trasta Bank, said.
Other official list stocks Riga Transport Fleet and Staburadze were stable at 1.77 lats and 2.70 lats.
Transport Fleet registered trade of 35,600 lats and Staburadze saw a small volume of 500 lats of shares.
Leading secondary list share Daugavpils Chain was in demand on volume of 20,300 lats. It slipped two santimes to 2.78 lats.
Kaija fish cannery, whose prospectus was today approved by the securities commission to enter the official list, added one santime to 2.41 lats on volume of 13,600 lats.
Lode Brick slipped to 2.35 from 2.50, losing most of the ground it gained after news of 1996 results and bonus shares.
"As soon as first quarter results come, confirming that everything is going according to plan, Lode will advance again," Trasta's Bulavs said.
"This is an interesting time as 1996 results and 1997 first quarter results overlap in many cases," he added.
